tweet_summary: Mike Nellis cites a handwritten 'J. Epstein' letter to Larry Nassar saying 'our president shares our love of young, nubile girls' as proof Trump is implicated in the latest Epstein DOJ release.
bad_note_text: The postcard is fake. DOJ and the FBI determined the card mentioning "our president" is inauthentic — it was postmarked Aug 13, 2019 (after Epstein's Aug 10 death) and was flagged by investigators. https://www.reuters.com/world/us/justice-department-releases-card-mentioning-trump-purportedly-sent-epstein-2025-12-23/
failure_reason: Substantively correct but could be sharper — leaves out two strong red flags (Virginia postmark, missing inmate number, handwriting mismatch). Reached NEEDS_MORE_RATINGS likely due to political polarization more than note quality.
why_note_decision: The DOJ and FBI determined this specific letter is fake (CNN, Axios, NewsNation, The Hill, Reuters): postmarked August 13, 2019 — three days after Epstein's August 10 suicide; postmarked in Virginia, not New York where he was held; the return address gives a different jail; the envelope lacks Epstein's required inmate number; handwriting does not match. Jail staff flagged it to the FBI at the time. Many comments on the post already note the post-death postmark. A note is clearly warranted on a ~99K-view post presenting fabricated evidence as a Trump-Epstein smoking gun.

tweet_summary: Profanity-laden meme posted as 'Sincerely, The American People' asserting foreign exporters — not Americans — pay U.S. tariffs, plus a claim about an automatic 15% 'fuck you globalists' tax renewed every 149.5 days.
bad_note_text: Importers, not foreign exporters, pay U.S. tariffs at Customs; research shows those costs are often passed on to American businesses and consumers. Claims of an automatic 149.5-day 15% renewal lack supporting evidence. https://www.cfr.org/articles/who-pays-trumps-tariffs
failure_reason: Substantively correct on the headline claim, but the dismissal of the 150-day point as 'lacking supporting evidence' is itself loose — Section 122's 150-day cap is real, the meme just garbles it. Note also a bit thin on sources for a contested political claim (only one link).
why_note_decision: The core claim ('foreign exporters paid tariffs, not Americans') is straightforwardly false. U.S. tariffs are levied at Customs on importers of record, who almost always pass at least part of the cost through to U.S. businesses and consumers (CFR, Tax Foundation, PIIE; widely documented for the 2018-19 and 2025-26 tariff rounds). The '149.5-day 15%' framing garbles a real mechanism — Section 122 of the Trade Act lets the President impose tariffs up to 15% for up to 150 days without Congress — but distorts it (it's not 'auto-renewed every 149.5 days'; Congress must extend).
